findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done - The full owner-approved item is: "forge hook context finishes in about 2 seconds or less on a repo with many hotspots, prints at most a few hotspot lines with a pointer to the full list, and worker rounds start without an initialize timeout".
Case: normal use - a client repository has spotted items and its Git remote is slow or unavailable. This call reaches `spotted.before_signoff` (`src/forge/spotted.py:144`), which calls `repo.default_config`; that function performs `git fetch` without a timeout (`src/forge/repo.py:721-725`, `222-224`). The hook can therefore exceed the startup deadline again, or exit before printing any context when the fetch fails. The reported 1.6-second measurement on this repository does not cover a slow remote.
findings.title: Not done: forge hook context finishes in about 2 seconds or less on a repo with many hotspots

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Gate - The new context output leaves existing tests asserting the removed output.
Case: normal use - the repository runs its related or full test suite. `tests/test_contracts.py:364-366` still requires session context to start with the complete `forge next` output for both hosts, and `tests/test_contracts.py:414-416` requires it to contain "waiting for approval". For their normal ready-story fixtures, this changed line prints the pointer instead, so those tests fail. Update both contract checks for the approved shorter output.
findings.title: Gate: update the session-start host contract tests

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test - The named proof checks the displayed lines but neither the elapsed time nor worker initialization.
Case: normal use - a Claude worker starts in a client repository with many hotspots. A hook that takes 30 seconds and then prints the same text still passes this test, as does a broken worker startup, because it never starts a worker. The fixture also uses a Forge source repo (`tests/test_story.py:137-141`), so it bypasses the client sign-off scan in `src/forge/spotted.py:144-160`. The one-off timing measurement does not provide a regression check for these Done-when details.

findings.body:

Raise: Test - The changed human-touch checks now read private `.factory` JSON records directly here and in `tests/test_approval_pin_notice.py:83-84`.
Case: normal use - an answered question contributes to the reported human-touch measure. These assertions can pass while the reported aggregation is wrong, and a storage refactor can break them while the reported behavior remains correct. The test audit requires these checks at the user-visible Forge boundary.

findings.body:

Raise: Gate - The repository's review rule requires each Forge change to say what a new client repo and an existing client repo on upgrade each receive.
Case: normal use - a client initializes Forge or upgrades to this release. The change's proof and commit messages describe the shorter hook generally but do not state the result for each client-repo path. The earlier-adopted fixture in `tests/test_handover_notes.py:12-19` does not describe an upgrade. Record the release effect for both paths.
